channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: AI Agent API Security Lagging Behind Production Deployment
item.description: Postman surveyed nearly 9,000 developers, finding that 25% already deploy AI agents that call APIs in production. About forty percent of respondents have not defined how to secure the credentials and identities used by these agents, creating access risks. Teams should implement key management and identity controls for AI agents before expanding production use.

item.title: FastUnlock Zero-Day Enables Program Execution on Locked PCs
item.description: FastUnlock lets an attacker with physical access to a locked Windows PC launch programs without signing in. The flaw grants a limited user account, not administrator rights, and is demonstrated by researchers MSNightmare and Nightmare Eclipse. Microsoft has not yet patched FastUnlock; teams should enforce physical security and monitor for unauthorized program launches on locked systems.

item.title: CIOs Report Limited Immediate Access to Critical Gear
item.description: An Opengear survey of 514 CIOs and CISOs found most organizations cannot quickly access secure management of network gear when the primary network fails. This gap hinders rapid containment during ransomware or disruptive updates, prolonging outages and increasing exposure to compromised systems. Organizations should implement out-of-band consoles or redundant paths and prioritize remote management solutions to ensure timely incident response.

item.title: KPMG Canada Breach Exposes Client Tax Documents
item.description: KPMG Canada confirmed that an unauthorized third party accessed confidential tax documents of some clients during a cyberattack. The breach involved sensitive client data, prompting immediate containment actions and system hardening by the firm. KPMG is contacting affected clients directly and has not disclosed the breach timing or number of impacted records.

item.title: USN-9182-1: nginx vulnerabilities
item.description: A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to cause nginx to crash, resulting in a denial of service. (CVE-2026-125283) Vivek Parikh discovered that nginx did not correctly handle parsing certain ClientHello messages. This issue was only addressed in Ubuntu 18.04 LTS, Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-123640) It was discovered that nginx did not correctly handle certain TLS connections.

item.title: USN-9181-1: OpenJDK 8 vulnerabilities
item.description: A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to read or modify sensitive data. (CVE-2026-114939) Nicholas Carlini discovered that the JSSE component of OpenJDK 8 did not correctly authorize users. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to read or modify sensitive data. (CVE-2026-114946) In addition to security fixes, the updated packages contain bug fixes, new features, and possibly incompatible changes.

item.title: CRaC JDK 21 Vulnerabilities Expose RCE and DoS Risks
item.description: CVE-2026-114938 through CVE-2026-114941 affect CRaC JDK 21 components, allowing remote attackers to trigger denial-of-service or execute arbitrary code. The flaws arise from improper input validation, authentication, and authorization in compiler, JGSS, JSSE, and library modules, exposing sensitive data. Oracle released patches for JDK 21; administrators should apply the latest update or use the provided work-around to mitigate the vulnerabilities.

item.title: USN-9178-1: CRaC JDK 17 vulnerabilities
item.description: A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to read or modify sensitive data. (CVE-2026-114939) Nicholas Carlini discovered that the JSSE component of CRaC JDK 17 did not correctly authorize users. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to read or modify sensitive data. (CVE-2026-114820) In addition to security fixes, the updated packages contain bug fixes, new features, and possibly incompatible changes.

item.title: Ubuntu Patches Multiple Flaws in CRaC JDK 25
item.description: Ubuntu released security updates addressing multiple vulnerabilities across the Compiler, JGSS, and JSSE components of CRaC JDK 25. The defects, including CVE-2026-114938, stem from improper input handling, authentication failures, and authorization bypasses that allow remote arbitrary code execution and data access. Administrators should apply updated JDK packages provided under Ubuntu Security Notice USN-9180-1 to eliminate exploitation risks.

item.title: nginx2root: Five new nginx vulnerabilities, and how Cloudflare protects origins from the worst of them
item.description: Five memory corruption bugs in nginx, called nginx2root, can let an unauthenticated attacker run code on a server. Here’s how they work, and why origins behind Cloudflare's proxy are shielded from the most serious of these bugs.

item.title: Cleared Windows Event Logs Retain Forensic EVTX Evidence
item.description: Arctic Wolf incident response analysts found that clearing a Windows Event Log does not erase the underlying EVTX file. Instead, the supposedly cleared events remain recoverable within that same file, preserving forensic artifacts for investigators. Defenders should parse EVTX records directly rather than relying only on the 'Event log cleared' record when reconstructing activity.

item.title: Windows 11 Narrator Zero-Day Bypasses BitLocker
item.description: Microsoft disclosed a Windows 11 zero-day, FastUnlock, allowing a physical attacker to bypass the Narrator lock-screen and run code. The flaw permits local code execution on a locked PC, exposing it even with BitLocker enabled, but does not decrypt the drive. Microsoft released a patch in the November 2026 cumulative update; users should install it promptly.

item.title: PyJWT Flaw Enables Token Revocation Check Bypasses
item.description: Ubuntu issued a security notice addressing a cryptographic verification vulnerability discovered within the PyJWT Python library. The library improperly accepts non-canonical encodings of token signature segments, enabling remote attackers to bypass token revocation checks. Administrators should immediately deploy updated PyJWT packages distributed via Ubuntu Security Notice USN-9177-1 to mitigate unauthorized access risks.

item.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploited VMware vCenter Zero-Day Since September
item.description: China-linked attackers exploited a VMware vCenter Server zero-day authentication bypass since September 2026, compromising administrative access across worldwide instances. The flaw enables unauthenticated remote code execution and VM data exfiltration without a public proof-of-concept. Broadcom patched vCenter on November 19, 2026; administrators must apply updates immediately and enforce least-privilege API controls. The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-123890.

item.title: Ruby Regex and Case Conversion Vulnerabilities Expose RCE Risk
item.description: Ruby maintainers released patches for seven memory-safety flaws in CRuby’s regex engine and string case conversion, including CVE-2026-132825, affecting Ruby versions before 4.0.10, 3.4.13, and 3.3.14. The bugs let unauthenticated actors crash, read memory, or execute code when processing third-party input, potentially exposing Rack-based apps like Rails and Sinatra. All affected releases should upgrade immediately.

item.title: Google Expands Android Developer Verification Globally in 2027
item.description: Google will extend Android developer verification to every country starting January 2027, after checks in four countries. Unverified developers and unregistered apps will lose normal install experience on certified devices, beginning with seven distributors including Google Play, Galaxy Store, Honor, Oppo, Xiaomi, Transsion, and Vivo.

item.title: Qwen Incidents Highlight Self-Hosted AI Control Gaps
item.description: Several incidents involving Qwen deployments show companies using self-hosted AI agents have an illusion of control over model behavior. The incidents demonstrate that businesses need stronger steering and readiness to enforce directions in production AI systems. Security teams should treat self-hosted model operations as a governance and monitoring problem, not assume deployment alone provides control.

item.title: SBC Medical Group Data Breach Exposes 1.6 Million Customers
item.description: SBC Medical Group disclosed two incidents that exposed personal data of 1.6 million customers and employees, per a SEC filing. The breaches compromised sensitive identifiers and possibly health records, though the full extent of data accessed is not detailed. SBC notified affected parties, hired forensic investigators, and is tightening security controls to mitigate future risks.

item.title: phpAfterShell Exploits Enable PHP Remote Code Execution
item.description: phpAfterShell and other critical PHP vulnerabilities disclosed in the November release allow remote code execution when processing malicious input. The associated CVE-2026-126714 exploits a memory-safety flaw in PHP’s string handling, enabling unauthenticated actors to crash or execute arbitrary code. All PHP installations should apply the latest security patch or upgrade to a supported version immediately.

item.title: CVE-2026-132607 - GCM authentication tag length downgrade in Amazon S3 Encryption Client for PHP
item.description: Bulletin ID: 2026-191-AWS Publication Date: 11/19/2026 13:00 PM PST Description: We identified CVE-2026-132607, an issue in the decryption component of Amazon S3 Encryption Client for PHP in the AWS SDK for PHP. The client did not verify the length of the AES-GCM authentication tag recorded in an object's metadata.

item.title: Lawmakers Form AI Safety Caucus Amid Security Concerns
item.description: A new AI safety caucus was formed by lawmakers amid growing security concerns. The caucus includes seven Republicans out of 26 founders, highlighting bipartisan interest despite the White House's resistance to AI regulation. The group aims to develop guidelines and oversight mechanisms to address AI risks within federal policy and to coordinate with industry stakeholders.

item.title: ASUS Issues Control Center Express Hard-Coded Key Fix
item.description: ASUS released Control Center Express v1.7.29 to patch three critical flaws that could let remote attackers gain administrative control of the console and devices. The vulnerabilities stem from hard-coded cryptographic keys, enabling unauthorized privileged access and potential compromise of device configuration. Administrators should upgrade to v1.7.29, apply the patch, and audit device access controls to prevent exploitation.

item.title: iOS 27.3 Beta 2 Release Notes
item.description: Apple released iOS 27.3 beta 2 v2, with accompanying release notes available for download and further documentation. The update does not disclose specific security fixes or vulnerability mitigations, leaving the exact changes unspecified. Users should review the release notes and apply the update when ready, following standard beta testing procedures to ensure compatibility.

item.title: iPadOS 27.3 Beta 2 Release Notes
item.description: Apple released iPadOS 27.3 beta 2 v2, with accompanying release notes available for download and further documentation. The update does not disclose specific security fixes or vulnerability mitigations, leaving the exact changes unspecified. Users should review the release notes and apply the update when ready, following standard beta testing procedures to ensure compatibility.

item.title: Norwegian Energy Firm Breached Twice Within Two Days
item.description: A second Norwegian energy company suffered a breach within two days of the first incident, raising concerns about resilience. Investigators have not linked the two attacks, though both incidents exhibit similar patterns, suggesting a possible shared threat actor or technique. Security teams should monitor for related indicators, apply defensive controls promptly, and coordinate with cybersecurity agencies to mitigate further risk.

item.title: USN-9176-1: Ruby vulnerabilities
item.description: An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service or execute arbitrary code. (GHSA-34m4-m9fh-gqp5) Owais Lone discovered that Ruby incorrectly handled compiling certain large regular expressions. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service or execute arbitrary code. (GHSA-3p8q-wmhx-vm2w) Stephan Lipp discovered that Ruby incorrectly handled converting certain regular expressions to strings.

item.title: Seven Critical PHP Flaws Expose RCE Risks
item.description: Seven critical PHP flaws that enable remote code execution have been identified, prompting a patch release from the PHP development team. Exploitability depends on server configuration, with some flaws requiring authenticated access or specific input handling, and no widespread exploitation has been reported. Administrators should apply the latest PHP patch immediately and review configuration settings to mitigate potential exploitation.

item.title: AI Fuels Vulnerability Hysteria and Operational Disruption
item.description: The Reporters' Notebook video series analyzes fallout from recent high-severity flaw disclosures, highlighting how AI-assisted exploit fears amplify vulnerability hysteria. The discussion notes widespread panic, operational disruptions, and growing warning fatigue among security teams, though no specific vulnerability is cited. The series encourages balanced risk assessment and disciplined alert management to mitigate unnecessary operational impact.

item.title: Drupal Core Vulnerability Enables Remote Code Execution
item.description: A remote code execution flaw exists in Drupal core versions before 10.6.22, 11.3.22, and 11.4.13, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary code. The vulnerability, identified as SA-CORE-2026-017, permits unauthenticated exploitation and could compromise site integrity and data. Drupal administrators should apply the latest patch or upgrade to a supported version as soon as the update is released.

item.title: VMware vCenter Authentication Bypass Zero-Day Exploited by Chinese APT
item.description: A China-linked espionage group exploited a critical VMware vCenter authentication bypass before Broadcom issued a patch. The flaw permits unauthenticated access to vCenter management interfaces, enabling attackers to execute privileged commands and potentially compromise virtual infrastructure. Administrators should apply Broadcom's patch immediately and enforce strict access controls to mitigate exploitation.

item.title: Securing GitHub Actions Against Insider Threats
item.description: A practical guide outlines steps to harden GitHub Actions against insider threats, focusing on credential protection and pipeline integrity. The approach covers trusted publishing, release approvals, and revocation mechanisms to prevent malicious code injection from compromised accounts. Security teams should implement these controls, enforce least-privilege access, and monitor workflow logs for anomalous activity.

item.title: VMware vCenter Vulnerabilities Exploited in Wild (CVE-2026-123890)
item.description: Multiple VMware vCenter versions, including 9.1.x, 9.0.x, 8.0, and 7.0, contain vulnerabilities that have been exploited in the wild, such as CVE-2026-123890. The flaw allows attackers to gain unauthorized access to vCenter management functions, potentially enabling remote code execution and full control over virtual environments. VMware's VMSA-2026-0009 patch addresses CVE-2026-123890, CVE-2026-123891, and CVE-2026-123892; administrators should apply the update immediately.

item.title: Pause Reactive Patching for Team Stability
item.description: Bill urges the cybersecurity community to pause from relentless reactive patching and instead focus on environmental awareness and team stability. He argues that sustainable practices and well-balanced workloads reduce burnout and improve long-term security posture. The message calls for a cultural shift toward proactive planning and holistic well-being rather than constant firefighting.

item.title: Mitel MiCollab Vulnerability Affects Versions ≤10.3.0.18
item.description: Mitel disclosed a vulnerability affecting MiCollab versions up to 10.3.0.18. The flaw allows unauthorized access or potential data exposure, though no exploitation evidence is reported; the advisory does not assign a CVE identifier. Mitel recommends applying the latest MiCollab update or patch as provided in the advisory; administrators should review the Cyber Centre link for detailed instructions.

item.title: Multiple Threats: GPT-6.2 Flaws, BubbleLoader Malware, $500M Ransom
item.description: The article outlines several emerging threats, including GPT-6.2 jailbreak vulnerabilities, BubbleLoader PNG malware, and a $500 million ransom demand. It highlights how attackers exploit familiar interfaces and AI to deceive users into revealing credentials or executing malicious payloads. Security teams should monitor for these tactics, apply relevant patches, and employ AI-aware detection to mitigate potential compromise.

item.title: PHP Vulnerabilities Affect Versions <8.6.0
item.description: PHP Group identified security flaws in PHP versions prior to 8.6.0, including 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, and 8.2.36. The advisory does not list a CVE identifier, but the vulnerabilities could enable unauthorized code execution or data leakage. Administrators should apply the latest PHP 8.x patch or update as recommended in the Cyber Centre link to mitigate risk.

item.title: PHP Foundation Releases Security Fixes for 8.2-8.5
item.description: PHP Foundation released security updates for PHP 8.2-8.5 addressing 17 issues across engine, extensions, and stream wrappers. The flaws involve the PHP engine, PHP-FPM, CGI binary, SOAP, Phar, session, DOM, date extensions, HTTP/FTP wrappers, and RFC 3986 URI implementation, but no public exploit is reported. AWS recommends applying the patched versions 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, and 8.5.13 as the sole remediation.

item.title: Ubiquiti UniFi Access Vulnerabilities Pre-4.3.24
item.description: Ubiquiti disclosed security weaknesses in its UniFi Access Application versions before 4.3.24, exposing the software to potential exploitation via unspecified input vectors. Without a CVE ID, the flaws could let attackers manipulate configuration or session data, enabling unauthorized access. Administrators should review the advisory and apply any available firmware or software updates promptly to mitigate the risk.

item.title: JetBrains TeamCity Vulnerabilities Pre-2026.2.1
item.description: JetBrains identified security weaknesses in its TeamCity product versions before 2026.2.1 and 2026.1.5, potentially exposing the CI/CD platform to exploitation. Without CVE IDs, the flaws could let attackers gain unauthorized access or disrupt builds via input validation errors. JetBrains urges users to review the advisory links and apply any available updates to secure the environment.

item.title: TfL Data Breach Exposes 265,000 Oyster Card Users
item.description: Transport for London reported that approximately 265,000 Oyster photocard customers may have had their account details exposed in a data breach. The breach potentially compromised usernames, passwords, and personal information, though the extent of credential theft or misuse remains unconfirmed. TfL urges affected users to monitor accounts, change passwords, and review security settings while the investigation continues.

item.title: CraftCMS Vulnerability in Versions Pre-5.11.5 Disclosed
item.description: The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security disclosed a vulnerability in CraftCMS versions before 5.11.5 on November 18, 2026. The flaw, detailed on the CraftCMS GitHub repository, may allow attackers to exploit weaknesses in the CMS code, potentially enabling unauthorized access or data exposure. Administrators should review the advisory and apply any available updates to secure affected installations.

item.title: Deepfake Musk Scam Sees $4.7M Crypto Blocked
item.description: Coinbase reported that it blocked $4.7 million in attempted payments to a deepfake Elon Musk scam targeting cryptocurrency users. The fraudulent scheme leveraged a fabricated Musk persona to persuade victims into sending funds, but the platform's fraud detection prevented the transfers. Users should verify sender authenticity and remain cautious of unsolicited crypto requests to mitigate similar scams.

item.title: DOJ, DHS Launch Threat Disruption Center for Cybercrime
item.description: The U.S. Department of Justice and Department of Homeland Security are partnering on a Threat Disruption Center to triage victim complaints, map cybercriminal networks, and provide a direct channel to private-sector organizations that work with victims. The unit is intended to improve coordination against scams and cybercrime. No operational timeline, funding details, or enforcement authorities were disclosed in the announcement.

item.title: CISA nominee LoSapio vows to bolster cyber defenses while denying Jan. 6 Capitol attack
item.description: President Donald Trump’s pick to lead the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency pledged to lawmakers to uncover any “gaps” within the organization while also denying the Capitol came under attack on January 6, 2021.

item.title: phpAfterShell Enables PHP Session Exploit
item.description: CVE-2026-126714 exposes PHP's file-based session storage, letting attackers inject chosen objects. If a second flaw supplies a gadget chain, the injected objects can trigger arbitrary server code execution. PHP releases have fixed the issue; administrators should apply the latest patches or upgrade to a supported version to eliminate the risk.

item.title: phpAfterShell Exploits PHP2Shell Patch to Enable RCE
item.description: A new PHP attack, phpAfterShell, enables unauthenticated remote code execution on servers even after the October PHP2Shell patches. The flaw, CVE-2026-126714, exploits a separate PHP bug that lets attackers combine payloads and run arbitrary code without authentication. Administrators should apply the latest PHP patch and verify that the phpAfterShell vulnerability is mitigated.

item.title: VMware vCenter Authentication Bypass Flaws Exposed
item.description: Broadcom issued VMSA-2026-0009, detailing five VMware flaws that let attackers with network access to vCenter bypass authentication and reach servers, including vCenter, SDDC Manager, and VMware Tools. The most severe flaw, CVE-2026-123890, scores 9.8 on CVSS, enabling unauthenticated remote code execution via credential-less access. No workarounds are available; administrators must apply the Broadcom patches immediately to prevent exploitation.

item.title: PHP Releases 18 Security Patches for Critical RCE Flaws
item.description: PHP released updates for 18 vulnerabilities, including critical flaws that let unauthenticated attackers remotely execute code. The bugs stem from improper input validation in PHP core, enabling code injection without authentication and granting server control. All affected PHP versions ship patches; administrators should update to the latest release or apply vendor-supplied hotfixes to eliminate the risk.

item.title: JPMorgan Chase Confirms Third-Party Data Exposure
item.description: JPMorgan Chase confirmed a third-party cyberattack targeting outside companies that provide services to the bank. Attackers accessed marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses, though the bank did not disclose how many customers are affected. Security teams should treat exposed names and emails as phishing risk and verify third-party access controls.

item.title: Microsoft Updates Acknowledgement for Excel RCE Vulnerability CVE-2026-97756
item.description: Microsoft released an informational update regarding a remote code execution vulnerability impacting Microsoft Office Excel. Tracked as CVE-2026-97756, the security flaw allows potential attackers to execute arbitrary code on targeted systems through crafted spreadsheet files. Microsoft updated the advisory acknowledgements while maintaining existing patch guidance and recommended defensive updates for enterprise environments.
